question: GQ-007
subject: reading the corpus instead of the plumbing
why: 78 books entered the Library today and I had verified schemas, counts and pages — never content. An unread book is inventory, not a library.

what_the_library_actually_acquired.dominant_strand: 18th-century London Magazine runs (1742-1779) and Victorian domestic-economy encyclopaedias
what_the_library_actually_acquired.five_serial_volumes: ~2.2M words alone — this is what the "Essays" tier really contained
what_the_library_actually_acquired.verified_by_reading: 1742 editorial voice on the reporting of parliamentary debates, and the preface to An Encyclopaedia of Domestic Economy

defect_i_shipped_an_hour_ago.cause: isHeading ran only on paragraphs that survived the >=120-char filter — and a heading is short BY DEFINITION. The two steps were in the wrong order, so the test could never see a heading.
defect_i_shipped_an_hour_ago.evidence: on one book, 39 blocks matched isHeading and all 39 were discarded before the test ran
defect_i_shipped_an_hour_ago.fix: mark headings during segmentation, before filtering

then_i_measured_the_quality_rather_than_.worst: "SIR," and "SIR ," labelling 2,996 passages — these books are full of published letters and an all-caps salutation passes every structural test
then_i_measured_the_quality_rather_than_.fix: excluded salutations BY NAME, not by length — "Book  V." is 8 characters and IS a heading, so a blunt length rule would have discarded real structure

a_corpus_limitation_i_am_recording_not_h.what: long-s OCR — 18th-century typography renders "such" as "fuch", "himself" as "himfelf"
a_corpus_limitation_i_am_recording_not_h.consequence: a search for "such" misses roughly half the matches; "himself" misses more than it finds
a_corpus_limitation_i_am_recording_not_h.not_fixed_deliberately: normalising f->s would corrupt genuine words (fuel, fund, fast) and is a transliteration decision about historical text, not a bug fix. Recorded so a reader knows the limit rather than trusting a silent index.
